goal: Determine whether post-build backbone maintenance needs a dedicated model or fits continuing FBM, without expanding FloRA's experiment.
procedure: Verify current branch tips and read post-activation builder scope before assigning a new model. Distinguish ongoing personal learning from construction and repair. Compare dedicated specialization with reuse of an existing FBM role, including training, resource and lifecycle costs. Read primary mechanisms and their transfer limits. Prefer an existing governed role provisionally; reserve specialist selection for matched independent defect and healthy-control evidence. Keep diagnosis, candidate construction, evaluation and promotion separate. Record a possible offline proposal-only comparison without adding it to the current behavioral experiment.
authority: Owner requested comparison of both optional maintenance routes and standing capture of reusable FBM methods; no runtime maintenance deployment was requested.
validation: Alice main, FBM and frontier-watch commit tips checked against remote; current FBM continuation and repair responsibilities read directly. SHAPER v2 method, DGM failure report, OpenEvolve evaluator source and Agent Lightning separation mechanism inspected. No model comparison, repair experiment, runtime test or latency measurement was run for this assessment.
failure_or_lesson: A separate responsibility does not establish the need for another trained model. Continued governed updates were already planned; implementation and repair competence remain unqualified. An optimizer must not edit its evaluator or activate its own patch on its own score. Existing semantic history is not complete telemetry, and background inference can still consume serving resources. Keep optional maintenance research separate from FloRA's frozen behavioral comparison. Source recovery initially hit Git cross-account ownership and wrong working-directory lookups; exact trusted-repository scoping restored reads without global configuration or architecture changes.
